accounts.name: What changed and why it matters

queue.body:
$WULF
6th rejection at the 50-day average (17.2) in a year.
Held 16.3, the most-traded price of the past six months.
4.2% above that shelf.
Below 14.2 the whole range is noise.

Jobless claims are averaging 203k a week this month, 13.1% below a year ago.
Atlanta Fed GDPNow has this quarter at 5.1% annualized.
Cleveland Fed median CPI running 2.1%.
The soft landing isn't a forecast anymore, it's the print.
$SIG fourth straight green week, tightest range in 7 sessions. Coiling under 100.

queue.headline: $SRE just lined up a pattern we track.
queue.body: Across every name we test it on, this combination has resolved higher 66% of the time about a month out over its full tested history, over 1990 occurrences universe-wide, not this one name. A measured tendency on a study split, not our trading record. Chart below.

accounts.name: Founder's desk: the day's tape, two facts set against each other

queue.body:
$PLMR dipped back to 136, the most-traded price of the past six months, and held.
That shelf capped every rally since April.
The weekly chart has moved into stalling out.
Jobs averaging 203k a week, 13.1% below last year, while GDPNow prints 5.1%. The soft landing stopped being a forecast and became the data.

featured_charts.headline: $TENX filing
featured_charts.body: Director Doogan Declan bought 53,000 shares of TENX at an average $1.92, roughly $102K. The purchase took the disclosed holding to 24x its previous size. The relative change is the part that matters, not the dollar headline.
